topic: The Leaf: Venation, Phyllotaxy and Modifications
title: Leaf Veins and Patterns Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A peepal leaf pressed in a notebook, a long blade of grass and a pea plant gripping the fence are all leaves. Diya asks: why does one leaf have a net of lines, another straight lines, and one turns into a spring?

You will see the parts of a typical leaf, zoom into reticulate venation down to the islands of green between veinlets, compare it with parallel venation, watch stems grow with alternate, opposite and whorled phyllotaxy, then leaf modifications: pea tendrils, cactus spines, onion and garlic, the Australian acacia petiole, the pitcher plant and the Venus flytrap. Then a pause and think check, a worked example, the exam trap, an original NEET match the following question and a recap card.

This is Episode 42 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.
